subject: HealthPlus security questionnaire: PII handling, dataflow diagram & subprocessor list
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@healthplus.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@healthplus.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security questionnaire & dataflow request — PII handling

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our procurement and security review I need a short SSQ focused on privacy/PII handling and an updated dataflow diagram that shows where tokens, embeddings, and logs live across regions. Key asks from our InfoSec team:

- PII categorization used by Redwood and how you map fields to categories (PII / Sensitive / Non-PII).
- Where customer prompts, generated outputs, and KV cache are stored (ephemeral vs persisted).
- KMS model: who holds keys, use of HSM, and whether keys ever leave our VPC (for Private deployments).
- Subprocessor roster for any components that process PII (with country of operation).
- Default retention windows for logs and generated artifacts and options for custom retention.
- Any cross-border transfer mechanisms (SCCs, adequacy, etc.) used for EU→US.

Can you send a short write-up (bullet answers) and a simple dataflow PDF we can attach to the SSQ? Ideally by EOD tomorrow — procurement has a tight timeline.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Security Operations
HealthPlus

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@healthplus.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Dataflow diagram + attachments for HealthPlus SSQ

Hi Elena — attached: a compact dataflow diagram (redaction_dataflow_v1.pdf) and our current subprocessor roster (subprocessor_roster_2026.csv). Highlights from the diagram (quick bullets):

- Prompt ingestion: TLS in transit, short-lived buffer on edge region, then routed to runtime.
- KV cache: in-memory on GPU hosts; optional cache persistence writes to encrypted blobstore when caching is enabled.
- Generated outputs: by default ephemeral and not persisted beyond session unless the customer opts into storage (e.g., for fine-tuning or audit logs).
- Logs & metrics: token-level aggregate metrics persist for 90 days by default; detailed request traces retained 30 days. We offer configurable retention for Dedicated/Private customers via Console.
- KMS: customer-managed keys supported for Private. Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS backed by HSM; keys do not leave the cloud provider's HSM. We can provide attestation excerpts on request.

Attachment stubs: [Attachment: redaction_dataflow_v1.pdf (diagram, 1 page)] [Attachment: subprocessor_roster_2026.csv]

Tell us if you want the diagram with additional callouts (e.g., token encryption at rest vs cache encryption).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@healthplus.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Subprocessor roster notes + quick answers to retention/KMS

Elena — following up with a few clarifying bullets that map to your InfoSec checklist. See attached CSV for full roster.

- Subprocessors that may process PII: storage provider, metrics/observability vendor, telemetry collector; all vendors listed in CSV and country column populated. We flag EU-located subprocessors in the CSV.
- Data exports & retention: by default Hosted retains request traces 30d / aggregates 90d; Dedicated customers can set retention via policy and Private customers control retention entirely.
- Cross-border transfers: Hosted operates under SCCs for EU customers and uses EU-hosted regions where required; Dedicated/Private customers can be configured to restrict routing to EU regions only.
- Key custody: for Hosted, Redwood manages KMS keys; for Private we support customer-provided KMS with HSM-backed keys. Keys for Hosted do not leave provider HSMs and are rotated per our cryptographic policy.

Attachment stub: [Attachment: subprocessor_roster_2026.csv]

If your team wants, we can produce a short addendum that enumerates subprocessors with data subdomains (prompts, outputs, logs). Happy to hop on a 20-min call to walk through.

-- Priyom
Security Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Torres <elena@healthplus.com>

Subject: Re: Security questionnaire & dataflow request — PII handling

Thanks team — this is really helpful and close to what we need. A couple of follow-ups before procurement moves to the next stage:

1) Can you confirm the default Hosted retention windows in writing (trace vs aggregate) so I can insert them into the SSQ?
2) For EU customers, are SCCs applied automatically or is there a contractual addendum? We need the legal mechanism documented.
3) We need a statement that generated outputs are not used for model training by Redwood unless explicitly authorized by the customer (plain language).
4) Please include redacted HSM attestation excerpt or pointer to where we can retrieve it.

If you can send a short (one-paragraph) response for each item and the final SSQ/DPA redlines by EOD Thursday, procurement can proceed. Also requesting a single-page diagram variant sized for inclusion in our vendor spreadsheet.

Best,
Elena
Head of Security Operations
HealthPlus
